reason: The mirage-deer (கானலைமான்) is a figure for worldly delusion; nothing about drugs from traditional texts.

The verse boasts that the Siddhars will turn the three worlds into red gold (செம்பொன் னாக்குவோம்); the finding that gold can be made from mercury only by nuclear reactions, never by alchemy, tells against the alchemical power claimed, though the boast is cosmic hyperbole rather than a stated procedure.

The verse says vaasi yoga completes pranayama (ப்ராணாயாமந் தீரும்) and removes obstacles to body-siddhi (காயசித்தி); HRV during slow breathing does not bear on a deathless body, so only breath practice is shared.
A long allegory of cultivating devotion in the heart's field; it names no medicine or metal, so the Siddha poisoning cases do not apply.
The poet does not know the breathing of life (உயிர்ப்பு) in the body; sun and moon becoming one are the two breaths only by cipher, and no claim about nostril alternation is made.
The verse asks to lie like a discarded corpse (கழிந்த பிணம்) with bleached bones while still seeing; death imagery is shared, but no claim about death reminders and attitudes.
A mother's wonder at a young girl's love for Ekambar; nothing about nostrils or brain hemispheres.
The body as a fort of nine gates (ஒன்பது வாயில்கொள் கோட்டை); no mercury or medicine.
A cipher of country legs and goat legs (ஆட்டுக்கால்); nothing about microbes.
The guru takes body, wealth and life by the rite of gift and changes karma; nothing about psilocybin or depression.

The poet failed to know the nature of ida and pingala (இடைபிங்கலை); the finding on single-nostril effects shares the left-right breath topic, but the verse makes no claim and the nostril reading is a gloss.
Questions about the five letters (அஞ்செழுத்து) and what their sword cuts; no claim about temperature or immunity.

The verse claims an atom of the substance cures all bodily disease (வியாதி யெல்லாம் ... பறந்து போகும்); artemisinin shows some traditional recipes hold real drugs, but that is not evidence about this preparation.

The verse claims that by the salt (உப்பதனால்) the body hardens and lasts for crores of aeons (கற்பாந்தங் கோடி காய மிதுவலுத்து) before old age (மூப்பு) turns it to calx; the finding that no hallmark of ageing has yet been reversed in humans tells against such a claim, though what the salt is is left in cipher and the syntax is broken.
The verse sums up causes and destruction (மாரணம்) as everything that comes also perishing; no metal preparations are named.
The eight-span body as a filth-nest (மலக்கூடு) that is still god's city; the microbial-body finding shares only the body-as-habitation theme.
The verse's one instruction is to be still (சும்மா இரு); a theory that meditation loosens predictive models shares the topic, but the verse makes no claim it tests.
The verse says the mind takes the bubble-body (நீர்க்குமிழி) for permanent; cell turnover shares only the body's impermanence.
The verse urges milking the unspoiling milk in the skull so as to live on (நாளும் இருந்திட); a longevity theme, but the milk is inner nectar by cipher and no lifespan claim is quantified.
A vow to eat only food brought to him, even if the body wastes (இளைத்தாலும்); eating and hunger are shared, but the verse claims nothing about metabolic effects of fasting.

The verse asks to cut down the dense forest of the mind (அடர்ந்த மனக்காட்டை) by striking again and again (தொடர்ந்து தொடர்ந்து) with the five-letter mantra; the finding that repeating a single word reduces widespread cortical activity bears on the idea that repetition quiets the mind, but it is speculative and does not settle the verse's claim.

The verse claims that holding the light of the root channel (மூலநாடி) for four nazhigai lets one live as a child (பாலனாகி வாழலாம்); voluntary autonomic control does not bear on rejuvenation, so only yogic practice is shared.
Creation traced from primal sound (சத்தம்) to Shanmuga and Ganapati; nothing about meditation and prediction.

The verse searches the body for the self and, by grace, tears the veil of maya (மாயப் படலங் கீறி); a model of psychedelics revising self-models shares the self theme but the verse's cause is grace, not a drug.
The verse says true learning is learning to be silent (பேசாது இருப்பது); meditation is the shared topic but no brain claim.
The Lord beyond the Vedas and the inner faculties (அந்தக் கரணம்); nothing about ageing.
A simile of the sun outshining the stars for the Lord's sight; not a report of meditative lights.
The medicine against dying (இறவாதிருக்க மருந்து) is remembering the Lord's feet; nothing about psilocybin.
The verse wishes to be contained in the letter a with va, ma and si (வவ்வெழுத்தும்); mantra is shared, but no claim of repetition or brain deactivation.

The verse mounts the vaasi gently in the silent five letters (மவுனஅஞ் செழுத்திலே வாசிஏறி மெள்ளவே) and ends in 'I am not'; mantra and breath are joined, but its claim is self-loss, and the finding concerns spoken recitation and baroreflex.

The verse traces something that flew, forgot, was born and at death found silence (மோனமே தெளிந்ததே); taken as the breath it shares breath and death with the finding, but there is no claim about a stock of breaths.
The verse calls giving up salt and eating once a day (அன்னம் ஓர்பொழுது) forms of desire; hedonic adaptation is unrelated.
The body is an unstable false cage (நிலையிலாப் பொய்க்கூடு); cell turnover shares only the body topic.
Desire for arts and siddhis (சித்துகற்கு மாசை) refuses to die; no claim about happiness returning to a set point.
Sun and moon (சந்திரனும் சூரியனும்) standing at the brow are the two breaths only by cipher; no claim about single-nostril effects on the brain.
The whirling gate (உழலும்வாசல்) opened to become the truth; nothing about Siddha decoctions.
Young men drawn by maidens' eyes to the bull-leaping; not mind-wandering in the finding's sense.
A silent yogi who does not rage; nothing about curcumin.
The moon changing (சோமன்மாறி) is breath moving between channels only by gloss, and the result claimed is the end of darkness and the flame-light seen (சுடரொளி), not blood pressure.
